acceptedAnswer.text: Edge bonding is generally a comfortable procedure. In most cases, local anaesthetic is not required because the treatment involves adding material to the tooth surface rather than removing tooth structure. Patients typically experience little or no discomfort during the process. The dentist works carefully to sculpt the composite resin, and the curing light used to harden the material is painless. If you have any concerns about comfort, your dental team will be happy to discuss options to help you feel at ease throughout the appointment.

mainEntity.name: How long does edge bonding last?

acceptedAnswer.text: The longevity of edge bonding varies depending on several factors, including the location of the bonding, dietary habits, oral hygiene, and whether you grind your teeth. With good care, composite bonding can typically last several years before any maintenance or replacement may be needed. It is worth noting that composite resin is not as hard as natural enamel or porcelain, so it may gradually wear or chip over time. Regular dental visits allow your dentist to monitor the bonding and carry out minor repairs if necessary, helping to extend its lifespan.

mainEntity.name: Can edge bonding fix all cases of short teeth?

acceptedAnswer.text: Edge bonding is suitable for many cases of mild to moderate tooth shortening, but it is not always the most appropriate option. In cases where teeth are severely worn, structurally compromised, or where there are significant bite concerns, alternative treatments such as porcelain veneers or crowns may be more suitable. The only way to determine the best approach is through a thorough clinical examination, where your dentist can assess the extent of wear, the health of the remaining tooth structure, and factors such as your bite alignment.

Modern composite resin materials are designed to closely mimic the colour, translucency, and texture of natural tooth enamel. A skilled dentist will select a shade that matches your existing teeth and sculpt the material to create a realistic, seamless appearance. When expertly applied and polished, composite bonding is generally very difficult to distinguish from the natural tooth. The aesthetic outcome depends on the quality of the materials used, the skill of the clinician, and the complexity of the case.

mainEntity.name: Does edge bonding damage natural teeth?

acceptedAnswer.text: One of the key advantages of edge bonding is that it is typically a non-invasive or minimally invasive procedure. Unlike some other cosmetic treatments, bonding usually does not require the removal of healthy enamel. The composite material is bonded directly onto the existing tooth surface after gentle preparation. This makes it a conservative option that preserves your natural tooth structure. If the bonding ever needs to be removed or replaced in the future, your underlying tooth should remain largely unaffected.

mainEntity.name: How much does edge bonding cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: The cost of edge bonding varies depending on the number of teeth being treated, the complexity of the case, and the materials used. During your initial consultation, your dentist will provide a clear treatment plan that includes an outline of expected costs. It is advisable to discuss all financial considerations before proceeding with any treatment, so there are no surprises. Many patients find edge bonding to be a cost-effective option compared to more extensive cosmetic procedures, though the most suitable treatment should always be determined by clinical need.
